mainTopic: Matching pairs of animals (the יום הכפורים goats, the מצורע's lambs and birds, the תמיד and מוסף lambs), and liability for slaughtering the יום הכפורים goats outside the עזרה before the lottery
overview: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא about the two goats of יום הכפורים. The extra word ״שני״ teaches that the goats should ideally be identical, and the repeated word ״שעיר״ teaches that they are still valid if they are not. Because ״שני״ appears three times, we might have thought matching was essential (עיכובא). Now that it is not, the three ״שני״ teach that the goats should match in appearance, height, and value. The same pattern is then applied to the מצורע's lambs and birds. There the word ״תהיה״ could have made matching essential, and it still makes the rest of the מצורע's procedures מעכב. The גמרא asks whether the two lambs of the תמיד should also match, and answers that ״שנים ליום״ is needed to teach that each lamb is slaughtered facing the sun. The two lambs of מוסף שבת, however, should certainly match. A new ברייתא then rules on slaughtering the יום הכפורים goats outside the עזרה, before and after the הגרלה. רב חסדא explains that before the lottery the goats are fit to be the outer מוסף goat, because waiting until later on the same day is not 'lacking time.' רבינא begins to apply רב חסדא's idea to שמואל's rule about שלמים slaughtered before the היכל doors were opened, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'two' teaches the goats should be identical
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא derives from the extra word ״שני״ that the two goats should be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: "He shall take two goats." The plural word "goats" already means at least two. So why does the verse add "two"? To teach that both goats should be the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the word ״שני״ is extra, so it must teach something new: the goats should be identical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural ״שעירי״ already means two goats, so the number ״שני״ seems unnecessary. The ברייתא reads that extra word as 'two of the same kind,' meaning the goats should match.

steps.title: Why would we think non-identical goats are invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a special ריבוי was needed. One ״שני״ alone would only teach a preference, not a requirement that invalidates.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason they are valid is that the Torah included them. That implies that without this inclusion, I would have said they are invalid. But from where would we get that this requirement is essential?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: why did the Torah need to tell us that non-matching goats are valid? Nothing suggested they were invalid in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קדשים, a detail stated once is usually only למצוה (the ideal). Only a repeated detail is essential (לעכב). So one ״שני״ should never have made non-matching goats invalid, and the ריבוי seems pointless.

steps.title: Appearance, height, and value
steps.stepSummary: Each ״שני״ teaches a separate way the goats should match: in appearance, in height, and in price.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is for appearance, one is for height, and one is for value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each ״שני״ adds a different detail of how the goats should be alike, all as the ideal way (למצוה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition is not for עיכוב. It spreads 'sameness' across three areas: מראה (look), קומה (height), and דמים (price). Ideally the goats match in all three, but they are still valid if they do not.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״תהיה״ still applies to every other step of the מצורע's purification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ריבוי takes only the matching of the birds out of the rule. Every other detail of the מצורע's purification stays מעכב because of ״תהיה״.

keyTerms.meaning: Its procedures (from the word ״תהיה״)
A person afflicted with צרעת

steps.whatToRemember: For the מצורע's birds, as with his lambs, matching is preferred but not מעכב. ״תהיה״ keeps all the other details מעכב.

phrases.english: For the rest of the procedures of the metzora.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״תהיה״ makes all the other details of the מצורע's purification מעכב

steps.title: Should the daily lambs also have to match?
steps.stepSummary: If this reasoning works, the גמרא suggests applying it to the תמיד. ״כבשים״ already means two, so ״שנים״ would teach that they should ideally match, and ״כבש״ ״כבש״ would show that they are valid if they do not. So should matching be a מצוה for the תמיד too?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us say the same about the daily offerings. 'Lambs' already means at least two. So why does the verse say 'two'? To teach that both should be the same. And how do we know they are valid even if they are not the same? Because the verse says 'lamb,' 'lamb,' which includes them. So should we also require matching lambs for the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same method to the two lambs of the daily קרבן תמיד. This would create a new rule there, and the גמרא challenges whether that is really correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תמיד, the verse also says ״כבשים... שנים״, even though the plural ״כבשים״ already means two. Using the same logic, ״שנים״ should teach that the lambs must match for the מצוה, and the repeated ״כבש״ ״כבש״ should show they are still כשר if they do not. The גמרא asks whether matching should then really be a מצוה for the תמיד too. Step 18 answers that ״שנים״ there is needed for a different teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily קרבנות brought every morning and afternoon
The minimum meaning of the plural 'lambs' is two
Equal or matching
For the ideal fulfillment of the מצוה, though not מעכב

steps.confusionAlert: Even here, the suggestion is only about the ideal מצוה (לכתחילה). Mismatched lambs would still be כשר because of ״כבש״ ״כבש״.

phrases.english: If so, regarding the daily offerings as well,
let us say: 'lambs' —
the minimum of 'lambs' is two,
so why does the verse say 'two'?
To teach that the two should be equal.
And from where do we know that even though
the two are not equal, they are valid?
The verse says 'lamb,' 'lamb,' which includes them.
So for the מצוה, do we indeed require (matching lambs)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, גַּבֵּי תְמִידִין נָמֵי, נֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the method of steps 12 to 16 to the קרבן תמיד
steps.kashyaTarget: How consistently the ״שנים״ derivation is applied
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an extra ״שנים״ teaches matching, the תמיד verse has the same wording. Yet matching lambs is not known as a מצוה for the תמיד.

steps.title: ״שנים״ for the תמיד teaches facing the sun
steps.stepSummary: The word ״שנים״ for the תמיד is needed for a ברייתא: ״שנים ליום״ means the lambs are slaughtered facing the position of the sun at that time of day.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed for what a ברייתא taught: 'Two per day' means opposite the day, that is, facing where the sun is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for the תמיד, ״שנים״ already has a different job. So it cannot teach that the lambs must match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that is already used for one דרשה is not free to teach another one. ״שנים ליום״ is read as ״כנגד היום″. The morning תמיד is slaughtered facing east, and the afternoon תמיד facing west, toward where the sun is. Because of this, there is no extra word to teach matching for the תמיד.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
As was taught in a ברייתא
Facing the day, meaning toward the sun's position

steps.whatToRemember: The matching rule from the extra ״שני״ applies to the שעירים of יום הכיפורים and to the מצורע's lambs and birds. It does not apply to the תמיד, because there ״שנים ליום״ teaches that the lambs are slaughtered facing the sun.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of how the גמרא reads verses: one word does not normally teach two separate דרשות. A word used for one lesson cannot also be used for a different one.

phrases.english: That (word) is needed
for that which was taught in a baraita:
'Two per day' means facing the day (the sun's position).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is already used for a different דרשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״שנים″ for the תמיד teaches that the lambs should match
steps.terutzMaskana: ״שנים ליום″ teaches slaughtering the תמיד facing the sun, so it does not teach matching

steps.title: Does 'two for the day' mean facing the sun or just the daily obligation?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether ״שנים ליום״ teaches that the lambs face the sun, or whether it only teaches that two lambs are the daily obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means opposite the sun's position during the day? Or maybe it only means the obligation of the day, that two lambs must be brought each day?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests its own reading of ״שנים ליום״ by offering a simpler meaning. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of ״שנים ליום״ seems to be that two lambs are brought every day. If that is what it means, then the word ״שנים״ teaches nothing new about direction. So the ברייתא must show why the simple reading cannot be the purpose of the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Opposite the day, meaning facing where the sun is at that time
The daily obligation, meaning how many lambs must be brought each day
"Two for the day", the phrase in the פסוק about the תמיד

steps.confusionAlert: This question is still part of the ברייתא quoted in step 18. It is not a new challenge from the גמרא.

phrases.english: Do you say it means opposite the day (the sun's position),
phrases.notes: This is the reading the ברייתא just offered.

phrases.english: or does it only mean the obligation of the day?
phrases.notes: That is, two lambs are required each day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כְּנֶגֶד הַיּוֹם, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא חוֹבַת הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא tests the reading it gave in step 18 against a simpler alternative.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ״שנים ליום״ teaches the direction of slaughter or merely the daily count of two lambs.

steps.title: Another verse already gives the daily count, so 'two' teaches facing the sun
steps.stepSummary: A separate פסוק already says one lamb is brought in the morning and one in the afternoon, so ״שנים ליום״ must mean facing the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Torah says, "One lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the other lamb you shall offer in the afternoon," the daily obligation is already stated. So how do I fulfill the words "two for the day"? They mean opposite the sun's position during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The daily count is already written elsewhere, so ״שנים ליום״ must teach something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not repeat itself for nothing. Because the פסוק already counts one lamb in the morning and one in the afternoon, ״שנים ליום״ is free to teach a new law: each lamb is slaughtered according to where the sun is at that time. This confirms why ״שנים״ by the תמיד cannot be used to teach that the lambs must match.

keyTerms.meaning: In the afternoon, literally "between the evenings"
It is already stated
How do I fulfill this verse? This asks what an extra phrase comes to teach

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״אֶת הַכֶּבֶשׂ אֶחָד תַּעֲשֶׂה בַבֹּקֶר
phrases.english: When it says: "One lamb you shall offer in the morning
phrases.notes: במדבר כח:ד

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵת הַכֶּבֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִי תַּעֲשֶׂה בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם״,
phrases.english: and the second lamb you shall offer in the afternoon,"
the obligation of the day is already stated.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים ״שְׁנַיִם לַיּוֹם״ — כְּנֶגֶד הַיּוֹם.
phrases.english: So how do I fulfill "two for the day"? It means opposite the day (the sun).
phrases.notes: The extra phrase is used for a new teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question raised in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The daily count is stated in במדבר כח:ד, so ״שנים ליום״ teaches that each lamb is slaughtered according to the sun's position.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because ״שנים״ by the תמיד is used for this teaching, it is not available to teach that the lambs must match. This answers the challenge from step 17.

steps.title: Where each תמיד was slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The morning תמיד was slaughtered at the northwest corner of the מזבח, and the afternoon תמיד at the northeast corner, each on the second ring.
steps.simpleTranslation: How was this done? The morning תמיד was slaughtered at the northwest corner, on the second ring. The afternoon תמיד was slaughtered at the northeast corner, on the second ring.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains in practice what "opposite the sun" means. It gives the exact spot where each lamb was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the morning the sun is in the east, so the lamb was slaughtered on the western side, across from the sun. In the afternoon the sun is in the west, so the lamb was slaughtered on the eastern side. Both were slaughtered in the north, on one of the rings set into the floor that held the animals during שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: The morning daily offering
Corner (of the מזבח)
A ring in the floor of the עזרה, on the north side, used to hold animals for slaughter

phrases.english: How so?
phrases.notes: This asks how the rule worked in practice.

phrases.english: The morning daily offering was slaughtered

phrases.aramaic: עַל קֶרֶן צְפוֹנִית מַעֲרָבִית, עַל טַבַּעַת שְׁנִיָּה.
phrases.english: at the northwest corner, on the second ring.
phrases.notes: The western side is across from the morning sun in the east.

phrases.english: And the afternoon one was slaughtered

phrases.aramaic: עַל קֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית, עַל טַבַּעַת שְׁנִיָּה.
phrases.english: at the northeast corner, on the second ring.
phrases.notes: The eastern side is across from the afternoon sun in the west.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains how the rule derived in step 20 was carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Morning תמיד: northwest corner, second ring. Afternoon תמיד: northeast corner, second ring. Each faces the sun's position.

steps.title: The two lambs of the מוסף of שבת should certainly match
steps.stepSummary: By the מוסף of שבת, the extra word ״שנים״ is not needed for anything else, so it certainly teaches that the two lambs should match.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the additional offerings of שבת, the two lambs certainly need to be equal (matching).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic. The idea of step 17 does not apply to the תמיד, but it does apply to the מוסף of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of מוסף שבת says ״שני כבשים״. The word ״כבשים״ already means at least two, and ״שני״ there has no other teaching such as "facing the sun." So ״שני״ teaches that the lambs should match, as the best way to do the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The additional offerings brought on שבת
Certainly
Equal, matching (in appearance, height, and value)

steps.whatToRemember: By the תמיד, ״שנים״ teaches slaughtering according to the sun. By the מוסף of שבת, ״שנים״ teaches that the two lambs should match as a מצוה.
steps.confusionAlert: Matching here is the preferred way to do the מצוה (לכתחילה). It does not invalidate the offering. The lambs are still valid if they do not match.

phrases.english: The additional offerings of שבת:
the two certainly need to be equal.
phrases.notes: This is learned from the extra word ״שני״ in במדבר כח:ט.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּסָפִין שֶׁל שַׁבָּת, וַדַּאי צְרִיכִין שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that ״שנים״ by the תמיד has another use, the גמרא applies the reasoning of step 17 to the מוסף of שבת instead.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The extra ״שנים״ by the מוסף of שבת teaches that its two lambs should match לכתחילה.

steps.title: Slaughtering the two יום הכיפורים goats outside, before or after the lottery
steps.stepSummary: If the two goats are slaughtered outside the עזרה before the הגרלה, there is liability for both. After the הגרלה, there is liability only for the goat for ה׳, not the goat for עזאזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone slaughtered the two goats of יום הכיפורים outside the עזרה before the lots were drawn for them, he is liable for both. After the lots were drawn, he is liable for the goat for ה׳ and exempt for the goat for עזאזל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. It is about the punishment for slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה (שחוטי חוץ).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the הגרלה, each goat still counts as a קרבן, so slaughtering it outside brings liability. The next steps explain why: רב חסדא says each goat is fit to be the outer מוסף goat. After the הגרלה, the goat for עזאזל is set aside to be sent away, not offered on the מזבח, so slaughtering it outside does not bring liability. The goat for ה׳ is a real קרבן, so slaughtering it outside does.

keyTerms.meaning: The two goats of יום הכיפורים
Outside the עזרה, which is the law of שחוטי חוץ
Drew the lots (הגרלה) that decide which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל
Liable (here, to כרת)
The goat sent away to the wilderness, not offered on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the הגרלה changes the status of each goat. That point drives the discussion that follows.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי שְׂעִירֵי יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן בַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: The two goats of יום הכיפורים that he slaughtered outside,
before he drew lots on them:
he is liable for both of them.
phrases.notes: רב חסדא explains in the next steps why they count as fit before the lottery.

phrases.english: After he drew lots on them:
he is liable for the one for ה׳ (the Name),
and exempt for the one for עזאזל.
phrases.notes: It is not offered on the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts a new topic after the matching-animals discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the הגרלה, slaughtering both goats outside brings liability for both. After the הגרלה, there is liability only for the goat for ה׳, and exemption for the goat for עזאזל.

steps.title: For what are the goats fit before the lottery?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's ruling that before the הגרלה a person is liable for both goats, and asks what the goats are fit for at that point.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Before he drew lots on them, he is liable for both of them.' For what are they fit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again so it can ask a question about it. Before the הגרלה, neither goat is assigned to anything, so how can slaughtering them outside make a person liable?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person is only liable for שחוטי חוץ (slaughtering outside the עזרה) if the animal is fit to be offered inside the בית המקדש. Before the הגרלה, neither goat has been picked to be the goat for ה׳. So the גמרא wants to know which offering these goats are fit to be.

keyTerms.meaning: He drew lots (the הַגְרָלָה picks which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל)
Liable (here, for slaughtering outside the עזרה)
For what are they fit?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. The גמרא is quoting the ברייתא from step 23 again in order to ask about it.

phrases.english: Before he drew lots on them
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא from the previous step

phrases.english: he is liable for both of them.
For what are they fit?
phrases.notes: Liability requires the animal to be fit for the Temple

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind the ברייתא quoted in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which offering the goats are fit for before the הגרלה, which would explain the liability.

steps.title: רב חסדא: they are fit for the outer goat
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that before the lottery each goat is fit to be the מוסף goat, whose service is done outside the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Because each is fit to be the goat that is offered outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. Even before the הגרלה, each goat is fit to be used as the מוסף goat of יום כפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of goat on יום כפור. One is the 'inside' goat, whose blood is brought into the היכל and the קודש הקדשים. The other is the 'outside' goat, the מוסף, which is offered in the עזרה. The 'outside' goat does not need a lottery, so both goats are already fit for it, and that is why there is liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
Fit (for use as an offering)
The goat offered outside the היכל, which is the מוסף goat of יום כפור

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Since it is fit for the goat that is performed outside.
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means in the עזרה, outside the היכל, not outside the Temple

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הוֹאִיל וְרָאוּי לְשָׂעִיר הַנַּעֲשֶׂה בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Before the lottery the goats are fit to be the מוסף goat, so slaughtering them outside creates liability.

steps.title: They are not ready for the outer goat either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא: the goats cannot be the inside goat because the lottery is missing, but they cannot be the outside goat yet either, because the special service of the day has not been done.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the goat offered inside, that they are not fit for it because they lack the lottery? They are also not fit for the goat offered outside, because the service of the day is still missing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's answer. If something missing makes a goat unfit, then the goats should be unfit for the outside goat too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מוסף goat may only be offered after the main יום כפור service, called עבודת היום, has been done. So right now the goats are missing something for the outside goat as well. Why should 'missing the lottery' make a goat unfit while 'missing the day's service' does not?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
Inside (the goat whose blood is brought into the היכל)
Lacking, still missing something
The special יום כפור service that must come before the מוסף

phrases.english: And what is different about the goat performed inside
that they are not fit for it, because the lottery is missing?

phrases.aramaic: לְשָׂעִיר הַנַּעֲשֶׂה בַּחוּץ נָמֵי לָא חֲזֵי,
phrases.english: They are also not fit for the goat performed outside,
because they still lack the service of the day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the goats are fit for the outside goat before the lottery.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both options are missing something (the lottery or the day's service), so there is no reason to call them fit for one and unfit for the other.

steps.title: Waiting for later on the same day is not lacking time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא holds that an offering due later on the same day is not called 'lacking time'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא holds: There is no 'lacking time' within that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. Waiting for the day's service is only a matter of time on the same day, and that does not make the goats unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering counts as מחוסר זמן (lacking time) only if it belongs to a different day. Waiting a few hours on the correct day does not count. The lottery is different, because it is an act that must actually be done to the goats, so missing it does make them unfit for the inside goat.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, his opinion is
Lacking time, an offering whose proper time has not yet come
Within that same day

steps.whatToRemember: Waiting for later on the same day is not a problem. A missing action, like the lottery, is a problem.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda holds:
There is no 'lacking time' within that same day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases into two kinds: missing time on the same day versus missing an action.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any missing step, whether a time or an action, makes an offering unfit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Waiting for later on the same day does not make it unfit. Missing the lottery is like missing an action, which does.

steps.title: רבינא connects רב חסדא to closed Sanctuary doors
steps.stepSummary: רבינא builds on רב חסדא's idea that missing the lottery is like missing an action, and quotes שמואל's rule that שלמים slaughtered before the היכל doors were opened are disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Now that רב חסדא said that missing the lottery is like missing an action, consider what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: שלמים slaughtered before the doors of the היכל were opened are disqualified, as it says 'And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the אהל מועד', meaning when it is open and not when it is locked.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבינא takes רב חסדא's principle and brings in שמואל's ruling, so that he can apply the principle to it in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא showed that something done outside the animal itself, like a lottery, can count as a 'missing action'. שמואל teaches that שלמים must be slaughtered while the doors are open, based on the words 'entrance of the אהל מועד'. Opening the doors is also an act outside the animal, so רבינא is about to compare the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that he said (introduces building on an earlier ruling)
Lacking an action that still has to be done
Peace offerings
The doors of the היכל (Sanctuary)
Disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא's actual point has not been stated yet. This passage only sets it up, and the conclusion comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns רב חסדא's answer about the goats into a general rule that can be used for other offerings.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Now that Rav Chisda said
that lacking the lottery is like lacking an action,

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: then regarding what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
Peace offerings that one slaughtered before
the doors of the Sanctuary were opened are disqualified,
as it is said: 'And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting',
phrases.notes: ויקרא ג:ב

phrases.english: meaning when it is open,
and not when it is locked.
phrases.notes: רבינא's application continues in the next part of the גמרא

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the principle established in step 27 and begins to apply it to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quoted ruling of שמואל: שלמים slaughtered before the היכל doors were opened are disqualified. רבינא is setting up an application of רב חסדא's 'lacking an action' principle to this case.
